_source: ww_particles.json - The Wind Waker (GZLE01) JPA particle/visual-effect system, mined for the gcrip Godot remake. Two independent sources, cross-validated against each other: (a) the real ripped particle banks on the retail disc, parsed byte-for-byte by a JPA1 reader written for this survey; (b) the zeldaret/tww decompilation at Z:/memRip/sources/tww, which contains the ENTIRE JSystem JParticle library as matching, non-stubbed C++ (see _data.library_status). TOP-LEVEL KEYS: _source  - this string. _data    - where particle data lives on disc, the complete JPAC1-00 / JPA1 binary format (container, resource header, block header, and every block's field offsets), the enum decodes, and whether gcrip can parse it (it can; proof in _data.validation). _api     - how game code fires an effect: the three-layer dComIfGp_particle_set* API, its exact signatures, the draw groups, and the callback mechanism by which an emitter follows a moving actor or a skeleton joint. _ids     - the 16-bit effect-id space: bit layout (bank select / toon / projection), how the per-stage Pscene###.jpc banks are loaded, and a table joining every id present on disc to its decomp enumerator name and its renderer-facing summary. _priority- the effects that matter most for play, ranked by how often actor code fires them, each with full renderer-facing data parsed from the real .jpc. _godot   - concrete mapping onto Godot 4 GPUParticles3D / ParticleProcessMaterial: what maps 1:1, the unit and frame-rate conversions, and what needs a translation layer. CONVENTIONS: every factual claim carries a 'cite' or 'cites' field. A cite of the form '<path>:<line>' is a line in the read-only decomp at Z:/memRip/sources/tww. A cite of the form 'rip:<path>' is a file on the ripped disc / inside the retail ISO. A cite of 'parsed:<file>' means the value was read out of that real .jpc by the parser described in _data.format. 'confidence' is high/medium/low. Frame counts are 30 fps GameCube frames unless stated. Colours are [R,G,B,A] 0-255. Nothing in this file is invented: no block name, id or offset appears here that was not read from the decomp source or from disc bytes.

location.summary: 58 JPAResourceCollection (.jpc) files, all JPAC1-00. One always-resident common bank plus 57 per-stage/per-room scene banks. They are plain files in the disc FST - not inside RARC, not Yaz0-compressed - so a byte range read straight out of the ISO is a complete, valid .jpc.
location.iso: Z:/3d ripper/roms/Legend of Zelda, The - The Wind Waker (USA).iso
location.note_not_extracted: gcrip's ripper already CLASSIFIES these (kind='particle', fmt='JPC') but does not extract them, so Z:/3d ripper/out/rip/GZLE01/ contains no .jpc. They must be read from the ISO by disc_offset from the manifest.

largest_scene_bank.note: superset bank - every scene id found anywhere also appears here

location.scene_bank_naming: Pscene%03d.jpc, the %d being the stage's or room's particle number.

library_status.verdict: NOT STUBBED. The JSystem JParticle library is fully decompiled, matching C++ - 18 .cpp (4386 lines) and 18 .h (2298 lines). Zero hits for NONMATCHING / #pragma / asm / TODO / STUB across the whole directory; no asm tree; every function carries a dtk ROM address+size comment; all 18 translation units are real splits in config/GZLE01/splits.txt, i.e. compiled from source rather than linked from a prebuilt lib. Several files even carry `static void dummy()` rodata-ordering fakematches, which is a hallmark of a byte-matching decomp. Consequence: every field offset, flag bit and enum in this document was read out of real code, not guessed.
library_status.only_v1: This decomp supports JPAC1-00 ONLY; it rejects any other version string. There is no JPAC2-10 path (that is the Twilight Princess / Super Mario Galaxy revision).
not_present: No JPABlendMode enum - blend fields are small indices into GX lookup tables.
No colorLoopOfstMask identifier; the equivalent is mColLoopOffset/mTexLoopOffset.

The texture block's 4-char magic is never validated by the loader; the loader trusts texResNum and each block's size. The magic IS 'TEX1' in every byte of every retail bank (1874/1874 blocks), but that is a disc observation, not a code claim.

container.magic: JPAC1-00 (ASCII, 8 bytes; the loader checks it as two u32s 'JPAC' and '1-00')
fields: emtrResNum - number of JEFFjpa1 emitter resources
padding to 0x20 (zero in every retail bank)
container.layout: header(0x20) then emtrResNum resources back-to-back, then texResNum texture blocks back-to-back, to EOF. No offset table, no padding between records.

resource_header.size: 0x20 (the struct's named fields end at 0x1A; blocks begin at resource+0x20)
fields: unidentified; nonzero and varying in retail data
blockNum - number of blocks in this resource

unnamed in the decomp struct; in retail data it equals the resource's total byte size (header+blocks) for 186/193 of common.jpc and the block-bytes-only total for the other 7, so do NOT use it to advance - walk blocks by blockNum and block size
textureNum - number of u16 entries in TDB1
resID - the effect id; becomes the emitter's userIndex
resource_header.resid_note: resID at +0x18 is the SAME u16 the game passes to dComIfGp_particle_set. getByUserIndex does a linear scan comparing the full 16-bit value with no masking, so the flag bits 0x8000/0x4000/0x2000 are part of the stored key.

fields: size - TOTAL block size including this header; advance by it
payload begins here - ALL block field offsets below are relative to block+0x0C, except where explicitly stated otherwise
block_header.unknown_magics: fall through the switch and are skipped by size (none occur in retail data)

BEM1.role: JPADynamicsBlockData - the emitter: shape, spawn rate, particle lifetime, initial velocity, per-frame damping. Exactly one per resource; always 0xA0 bytes on disc.
BEM1.gotcha_emitter_dir: mEmitterDir is stored UNNORMALISED, typically as +/-32767.0 per axis (an s16 that the authoring tool wrote out as a float). Normalise it before use. Observed in every retail bank.

BSP1.role: JPABaseShapeData - everything the renderer needs: shape/billboard type, texture, blend mode, alpha compare, z mode, the prm/env colours and their keyframe ramps, and the texture-scroll animation. Exactly one per resource; 0x60-0x100 bytes on disc (the variation is the appended side tables).

side_tables.present_when: mTextureFlags bit0 set and key count > 0

side_tables.type: JPAColorRegAnmKey[prmAnmKeyNum], 6 bytes each: s16 frame @0x00, GXColor @0x02

ESP1.role: JPAExtraShapeData - the per-particle envelopes: alpha in/out, scale in/out, spin. Optional; always 0x80 bytes on disc when present (3344 of 3370 records have one).
ESP1.gotcha: scale in/out X and Y are INTERLEAVED (inX, outX, inY, outY), not grouped.

SSP1.role: JPASweepShapeData - child particles spawned from live parent particles (sparks off a flame, droplets off a splash). Optional; 0x60 bytes on disc; 430 of 3370 records.

ETX1.role: JPAExTexShapeData - indirect (framebuffer-distortion) texturing. This is the heat haze / motion blur. Optional; 0x40 bytes on disc; 179 of 3370 records.

flags.(>>2)&3: index into indMtxID[4] = {ITM_0, ITM_0, ITM_S0, ITM_T0}

KFA1.role: JPAKeyBlockData - keyframe curves that animate an EMITTER-level property over the emitter's own timeline (not per particle). Zero or more per resource; 1143 blocks across all banks.
fields: mID - which property this curve drives

key_array.element0: frame/time; the remaining 3 are value and tangents

FLD1.role: JPAFieldBlockData - a force field applied to every particle. Zero or more per resource; 3696 blocks across all banks; always 0x60 bytes on disc. This is where gravity, wind, attraction and turbulence live.
FLD1.no_id_on_disc: getID() is hardcoded to return 0 in the archive implementation - FLD1 carries no per-field id (include/JSystem/JParticle/JPAFieldBlock.h:54)

TDB1.role: Texture id table - maps this resource's local texture slots (mTextureIndex, mIndTextureID, the flipbook array, SSP1's mTextureIndex) to indices in the bank's global texture list. Exactly one per resource.
TDB1.layout: raw u16[textureNum] at BLOCK BASE + 0x0C; textureNum comes from resource+0x16

texture_block.magic: TEX1 (observed in all 1874 retail blocks; NOT validated by the loader)
layout: a standard 0x20-byte BTI/J3D texture header, image data following at header+0x20
texture_block.gcrip_note: Because TEX1+0x20 is a plain BTI header, gcrip's EXISTING gcrip.formats.bti parser and gcrip.formats.gx_texture decoder read these with zero new code.
texture_block.observed_formats_note: 1785 of 1874 are single-channel intensity/alpha masks. Particle textures are almost all greyscale stencils that get COLOURED at draw time from prmColor/envColor - see _godot.tev.
texture_block.observed_sizes: 4x4 up to 256x256; 32x32 is by far the most common

gx_tables.note: The blend/compare fields are indices into these static GX tables, not enums.

validation.what_was_done: A JPA1 parser was written from the offsets above and run over all 58 retail banks read straight out of the ISO.

results.exact_byte_accounting: 58/58 - walking header -> resources (by blockNum and per-block size) -> texture blocks lands exactly on EOF in every file, and the resource and texture counts match the container header emtrResNum/texResNum in every file.
results.texture_blocks_decoded_to_rgba: 1874/1874 via the existing gcrip.formats.bti + gcrip.formats.gx_texture, zero failures
results.enum_decode_sanity: 0 out-of-range shape types, 0 out-of-range blend factors, z-compare func is LEQUAL in 3370/3370 records, blend is exactly 3 distinct combos across all data (alpha 2358 / additive 992 / multiply 14, plus 6 with BM_NONE)
results.independent_cross_check: 1078 of the 1091 distinct on-disc effect ids match a named enumerator in the decomp's d_particle_name.h, and the names agree with the parsed texture names in every case inspected (ID_AK_JN_O_FIRE00 -> AK_honoo* flame frames; ID_AK_JN_TUBA00 -> AK_tuba00; ID_AK_JN_SIBOUSPIRIT -> AK_sibouSpirit00; ID_AK_JN_HAMON00 -> hamon2_02; ID_IT_JN_TR_HAHEN_A -> kinohahen00). Two sources that were parsed independently agreeing this closely is the strongest evidence here that the offsets are right.

validation.gcrip_verdict: gcrip CAN parse .jpc, and cheaply. It already classifies the format (classify.py:65) and already owns the BTI/GX texture decoder the texture blocks need. A new gcrip/formats/jpa.py of roughly 250 lines - the container walk plus the eight struct decoders in _data.format.blocks - is the whole job; the ripper additionally needs to EXTRACT files/res/Particle/ which it currently classifies but skips.
validation.unnamed_ids_note: 13 ids present in retail banks have no enumerator in d_particle_name.h; 0x8396-0x83A1 is a contiguous run, suggesting a block the decomp has not named yet rather than a parsing error.

_api.overview: Three layers. Actor code calls an inline global wrapper; the wrapper picks a draw group; one real function does the work and hands back a raw JPABaseEmitter*.

layer1_wrappers.canonical_signature: JPABaseEmitter* dComIfGp_particle_set(u16 particleID, const cXyz* pos, const csXyz* angle = NULL, const cXyz* scale = NULL, u8 alpha = 0xFF, dPa_levelEcallBack* pCallBack = NULL, s8 setupInfo = -1, const GXColor* pPrmColor = NULL, const GXColor* pEnvColor = NULL, const cXyz* pScale2D = NULL)
special_forms: (u16, const cXyz*, const csXyz* = NULL, const cXyz* = NULL, u8 alpha = 0xFF)
(u16, const cXyz*, const csXyz*, const cXyz*, u8, u16) -> void
(u16, cXyz*, u8 alpha = 0xFF, GXColor& prm = g_whiteColor, GXColor& env = g_whiteColor, int = 0) -> void
(int code, const cXyz*, const csXyz*, f32, f32, f32, dKy_tevstr_c*, int* i_return_id, int flag) - the ground-attribute footstep/landing helper
(u16, const cXyz*, const csXyz* = NULL, const cXyz* = NULL, u8 alpha = 0xFF)
layer1_wrappers.does_not_exist: There is NO dComIfGp_particle_setColor, no set_particle, no mDoParticle, and no dPa_control_c::setToonTexture anywhere in src/ or include/. Colour is passed as the pPrmColor/pEnvColor arguments, or driven by a dPa_setColorEcallBack (include/d/d_particle.h:371).

layer2_groups.meaning: The group is a draw bucket - it fixes when in the frame the emitter is rendered and what lighting/TEV setup it gets. Toon effects are tinted by the room's dKy_tevstr_c; Projection effects do the framebuffer-copy heat haze.

layer3_real_function.signature: JPABaseEmitter* dPa_control_c::set(u8 groupID, u16 userID, const cXyz* pos, const csXyz* angle, const cXyz* scale, u8 alpha, dPa_levelEcallBack* pCallBack, s8 setupInfo, const GXColor* prm, const GXColor* env, const cXyz* globalScale)
body_order: createSimpleEmitterID(pos, userID, groupID, getRM_ID(userID), NULL, NULL)
else if (userID & 0x4000): attach the shared kagerou (heat haze) callback
layer3_real_function.returns: JPABaseEmitter* - a RAW POINTER, NULL on failure. TWW has no integer emitter handle. Failure means the emitter pool is exhausted or the id is not in a currently-loaded bank; the JSystem layer logs 'JParticle::Couldn't Create Emitter!'.
layer3_real_function.setupInfo_note: s8 setupInfo is not generic. In practice callers pass fopAcM_GetRoomNo(this) so that dPa_smokeEcallBack can look up that room's dKy_tevstr_c for lighting.

jsystem_floor.call: JPAEmitterManager::createSimpleEmitterID(const TVec3<f32>&, u16 userID, u8 groupID, u8 rmID, JPACallBackBase<JPABaseEmitter*>*, JPACallBackBase2<...>*)
jsystem_floor.lookup: pResMgrArray[rmID]->getEmitterResource()->getByUserIndex(userID) - a LINEAR SCAN comparing the full u16 with no masking

lifetime_and_following.one_shot: The default. set() returns the emitter, the caller ignores it, and the emitter self-deletes once BEM1 mMaxFrame frames have elapsed and its last particle dies. A BEM1 mMaxFrame of 0 means the emitter never stops on its own.
lifetime_and_following.persistent_mechanism: A CALLBACK OBJECT OWNED BY VALUE INSIDE THE ACTOR STRUCT - not the actor pushing a position each frame. dPa_followEcallBack::setup() stores mpEmitter, calls becomeImmortalEmitter(), and CACHES RAW POINTERS to the actor's own cXyz/csXyz members. Its execute(), which JPA calls every frame, then does setGlobalTranslation(mPos->x, mPos->y, mPos->z) and setGlobalRotation. So the EMITTER PULLS the actor's position through the cached pointer; the actor does nothing per frame. end() -> becomeInvalidEmitter(); quitImmortalEmitter(); setEmitterCallBackPtr(NULL).
lifetime_and_following.consequence: Because the callback caches a pointer INTO the actor, the actor must own the callback by value and must call remove() in its _Delete.
actor_examples: include/d/actor/d_a_arrow.h:96 (mBlurFollowCb - the arrow's motion trail, fired at src/d/actor/d_a_arrow.cpp:194)
include/d/actor/d_a_bpw.h:106-126 (a boss with ~10 named follow callbacks)
callback_variants: spin attack - carries a cXyz* path sampled from the sword blur

joint_following.what: A second mechanism welds an emitter to a SKELETON JOINT rather than a position.
joint_following.make: makeEmitter(id, mtx, pos, scale) = end(); setMatrix(mtx); return dComIfGp_particle_setP1(id, pos, NULL, scale, 0xFF, this);
joint_following.callers_pass: mpCLModel->getAnmMtx(CL_JNT_...) - e.g. the baton tip at src/d/actor/d_a_player_tact.inc:275 and the charge glow on Link's left hand at src/d/actor/d_a_player_sword.inc:1713-1714

lifetime_and_following.not_present: There is no dPa_modelEcallBack. The model-particle path is instead dPa_modelEmitter_c / dPa_J3DmodelEmitter_c / dPa_modelControl_c (include/d/d_particle.h:236-269, :383-393), used for pot shards (src/d/d_particle.cpp:652).

call_site_census.note: Bosses dominate the raw counts. For a remake the high-value work is the small set of generic effects in _priority, which are fired from shared code paths that run constantly.

_ids.kind: 16-bit unsigned. Ids are C++ enumerators in an unnamed enum inside `namespace dPa_name`, NOT #defines and not numeric literals - every call site in src/ uses the symbolic name (a grep for dComIfGp_particle_set*(0x... across src/d/actor/ returns zero hits).

name_header_shape.common_enum: :32-236 (203 ids, 0x0000-0x0469, 'Particles in common.jpc. Always loaded regardless of scene.')
name_header_shape.scene_enum: :240-1175 (934 ids, 0x8058-0xA470, 'must be loaded by a scene's particle bank')
name_header_shape.id_arrays: extern u16 j_o_id[] (8 entries) and s_o_id[] (34 entries), defined src/d/d_particle_name.cpp:10 and :21 - the effects pre-created as 'simple' emitters at bank load

0x8000.meaning: BANK SELECT. 0 = common.jpc (always resident). 1 = the current stage's or room's Pscene###.jpc.
0x8000.code: u8 dPa_control_c::getRM_ID(u16 uid) { return (uid >> 15) & 0x01; } - used directly as the index into JPAEmitterManager::pResMgrArray[]

0x4000.meaning: PROJECTION group hint. dPa_control_c::set() auto-attaches the shared kagerou (heat-haze) callback when this bit is set and no callback was supplied.

0x2000.meaning: TOON group hint - the effect is drawn in the toon bucket and tinted by the room's light colour.

bit_layout.low_13_bits: A sequential index within the author's list. NOT a global index and NEVER masked off: the full u16 including the flag bits is what is stored as the resource's userIndex inside the .jpc and what getByUserIndex compares.

bit_layout_disc_confirmation.what: The bit meanings were independently confirmed from disc content alone, before the decomp evidence was in hand, by looking at what textures each group's resources use.

common/group2 (0x4000): 2 of 2 carry an ETX1 indirect block
scene/group2 (0xC000): 42 of 42 carry an ETX1 indirect block

bit_layout_disc_confirmation.conclusion: Every 0x4000/0xC000 id on disc is an indirect-texture (heat haze / blur) effect - 44 of 44, no exceptions. Group 1 is the toon bucket. The 2-bit group value 3 never occurs.

chars.4: type: 'n' normal, 't' toon (0x2000), 'p' projection (0x4000); the values '1'/'2'/'4' also occur and the header itself marks their meaning 'Unknown' at :20

naming_convention.known_collision: ID_SCENE_END = 0x8466 collides with ID_IT_SN_DEMO_KOUSEKI02 = 0x8466 (:27 vs :1167). ID_SCENE_END is used purely as an array terminator, e.g. 245 times in dItem_data::effect_info[] (src/d/d_item_data.cpp:9973 onward).

common.how: mDoDvdThd_toMainRam_c::create("/res/Particle/common.jpc", ...) then dComIfGp_particle_createCommon -> dPa_control_c::createCommon, which builds the JPAEmitterManager with pools (3000 particles, 150 emitters, 200) and pre-creates simple emitters for the 8 ids in dPa_name::j_o_id[]

scene.how: sprintf(name, "/res/Particle/Pscene%03d.jpc", i_no) in dPa_control_c::readScene; refcounted (a second caller just bumps mCount and asserts the same scene number). createRoomScene then installs the result as mEmitterMng->pResMgrArray[1] and pre-creates the 34 ids in dPa_name::s_o_id[], choosing each one's group from its 0x4000/0x2000 bits.
scene.stage_hook: dStage_stagInfo_GetParticleNo(...) -> dComIfGp_particle_readScene, committed in phase_4 via dComIfGp_particle_createScene (src/d/d_s_play.cpp:1302-1303, :1323)
scene.no_bank: i_no == 0xff means 'this stage/room has no scene bank' (src/d/d_particle.cpp:692-694)

bank_loading.consequence_for_remake: An id with bit 15 CLEAR always resolves. An id with bit 15 SET resolves only if the current stage/room happens to have loaded the Pscene bank containing it - which is why 859 of the 1091 distinct ids appear in more than one bank file (the same effect is duplicated into every scene that needs it). For a remake, prefer common-bank ids: they are the 178 always-available effects and they cover every generic action (hits, deaths, footsteps, water, fire, bombs).
bank_loading.framebuffer_hook: The only texture-patching hook is swapFrameBufferTexture(), which patches the framebuffer copy into the texture literally named 'AK_kagerouSwap00' in both banks - that is the heat haze, not a toon table (src/d/d_particle.cpp:635-642).

_ids.table_note: Every one of the 1091 distinct effect ids present on the retail disc. Values other than the name come from parsing the real .jpc; the name comes from d_particle_name.h. A null name means the id is on disc but the decomp has not named it.

_priority.ranking_basis: Ordered by the number of distinct dComIfGp_particle_set* call sites in the decomp that name the id (counted over src/d/actor/, src/d/d_cc_s.cpp, src/d/d_cc_uty.cpp and src/c/), restricted to effects that matter for ordinary play rather than one-off boss set pieces. Entries with call_sites=null are fired from a single SHARED code path (the disappear actor, the ground-attribute helper, the bomb, the player) whose runtime frequency is far higher than its call-site count; they are placed next to the effects they play with.
_priority.caveat: Call-site count is a proxy for authoring breadth, not for frames-on-screen. The four SIBOU* death effects have only ~16 call sites between them but run on every single enemy death in the game.
_priority.renderer_data_source: Every numeric field below was parsed out of the real files/res/Particle/common.jpc (or the named scene bank) read from the retail ISO. See _data.format for what each field means and _godot.mapping for how to consume it.

frame_rate.note: Every JPA time value (mLifeTime, mMaxFrame, mRate, ESP1 timings, KFA1 key frames) is in 30 fps frames. seconds = frames / 30.

particle_world_size.note: globalParticleScale defaults to (1,1,1) (JPAEmitter.cpp:174-176) and is what the `scale` / `pScale2D` arguments of dComIfGp_particle_set set. So a BSP1 mBaseSizeX of 1.0 is 25 world units wide with no caller scaling. This is the single most useful constant for making the sizes look right first try.

acceleration.reasoning: JPA integrates in units-per-frame and adds acceleration once per frame, so a FLD1 Gravity mag of 1.0 is 1 unit/frame^2 = 900 units/s^2.
acceleration.cross_check: game.gd:2192 already uses gravity -900 for what reads as one g, which is the same number this derivation produces for mag 1.0.
acceleration.confidence: medium - the unit derivation is sound and the cross-check agrees, but it was not read off a line of decomp code.

constants.colour: GXColor is RGBA8. Godot Color = component / 255.0. These are NOT sRGB-corrected in the original; if the remake renders linear, convert.

tev.why_it_matters: 1785 of 1874 particle textures on disc are single-channel intensity/alpha masks. The colour you see comes from a two-register TEV blend, not from the texture. A remake that just modulates by one colour will look flat and wrong. This is the single most important thing to port.
tev.stage_setup: One TEV stage: GXSetTevColorOp(ADD, TB_ZERO, CS_SCALE_1). GX evaluates out = d + (1-c)*a + c*b for the arg quad (a,b,c,d).

colour_presets.resolves_to: rgb = mix(env.rgb, prm.rgb, tex.rgb)  <-- THE COMMON ONE
colour_presets.note: The texture's luminance is a MIX FACTOR between two authored colours, giving the warm-core/cool-rim look of Wind Waker's flames, smoke and sparks.

colour_presets.resolves_to: rgb = prm.rgb (flat, texture contributes only through alpha)

tev.godot_advice: Write ONE particle shader with uniforms prm, env and an int preset, and drive prm/env per-instance through INSTANCE_CUSTOM or a per-emitter material. Preset 3 alone covers 58% of every effect in the game; presets 3, 5, 0 and 1 together cover 99.6%.

direct: mMaxFrame > 0 -> a finite burst of mMaxFrame frames; mMaxFrame == 0 -> the emitter runs until something kills it, i.e. one_shot = false. 1504 of 3370 records have mMaxFrame <= 0.
amount ~= ceil(rate * lifeTime) for a continuous emitter; for a burst, amount ~= ceil(rate * max(mMaxFrame, 1))
rateStep 0 and a one-frame mMaxFrame is a pure burst -> explosiveness 1.0
Point->POINT, Sphere->SPHERE, Cube->BOX, Circle->RING, Cylinder->RING (with height), Line->BOX with two near-zero extents, Torus->RING (no exact equivalent)
omni = radially outward, dir = along mEmitterDir, axis = along the emitter axis; sum the ones that are nonzero and widen min/max by mInitVelRndm. Multiply by 30 for units/second.
JPA multiplies velocity by mAirResist EVERY FRAME (a value of 1.0 = no drag). Godot damping is a linear subtraction, so this is only approximate: damping ~= (1 - mAirResist) * speed * 30

SRC_ALPHA/INV_SRC_ALPHA -> BLEND_MODE_MIX (2358 records); SRC_ALPHA/ONE -> BLEND_MODE_ADD (992); DST_COLOR/ZERO -> BLEND_MODE_MUL (14). Those three are the ENTIRE blend vocabulary of the game's particles.
z compare func is LEQUAL in 3370/3370 records; z UPDATE (depth write) is off in 1032 of 1091 distinct effects, so default to depth_draw_mode = DEPTH_DRAW_DISABLED
see _godot.tev - do NOT collapse to one colour

The keys are (s16 frame, RGBA8); the original BAKES them into a per-frame lookup table at load time by linear interpolation, holding the last key flat past the end. Rebuild that as a Gradient with offsets = frame / mColorRegAnmMaxFrm. 262 effects have a prm ramp, 166 an env ramp. Bake cite: src/JSystem/JParticle/JPABaseShape.cpp:83-125
ESP1 alpha in/out timings and values
alpha in the color_ramp, or ALPHA in a shader
in/out timings are normalised 0..1 fractions of the particle's own life. 498 of 1091 effects use it.
ESP1 scale in/out timings and values
1020 of 1091 effects use it, so this is not optional. Remember X and Y are interleaved.

SUB_EMITTER_CONSTANT for a steady drip, SUB_EMITTER_AT_END for a death burst; mTiming picks which. mInheritScale/Alpha/RGB map onto sub_emitter_keep_velocity plus manual colour setup. 128 of 1091 effects have a child.
BSP1 texture flipbook (mTextureAnmKeyNum + the u8 array at block+0x60)
StandardMaterial3D particles_anim_h_frames/v_frames with billboard_mode = BILLBOARD_PARTICLES and particles_animation = true

Godot DOES support flipbooks, but the frames must be packed into one atlas at rip time. 260 of 1091 effects animate their texture; frame counts observed are 2 (163 effects), 3 (47), 4 (9), 6, 8, 10 (17), 20 (19) and 30 (3).
gravity = mDir * mMag * 900 (see constants). 2327 of 3696 field blocks are Gravity - it is by far the common case.
Magnet is a linear pull toward mPos, Newton an inverse-square one. 188 + 223 blocks. Attractors are scene nodes, not material properties, so this costs a child node.
parent the GPUParticles3D to the actor node
Set local_coords = false so already-emitted particles stay behind in world space - that reproduces what dPa_followEcallBack does (it moves only the EMITTER, never live particles).

needs_translation_layer.why: A Stripe is not a cloud of billboards - it is ONE ribbon mesh threaded through every live particle in emission order, so the emitter draws a connected trail. Godot's GPUParticles3D has no equivalent; each particle is independent.
needs_translation_layer.suggestion: Do not use GPUParticles3D at all for these. Use an ImmediateMesh or a RibbonTrailMesh driven from GDScript over a ring buffer of recent positions. This is exactly what the original does for the spin attack: dPa_cutTurnEcallBack_c is handed a 10-entry cXyz array sampled from the sword blur path (src/d/actor/d_a_player_main.cpp:9998-10000). The Wind Waker baton trail and the arrow blur are the same problem.

needs_translation_layer.what: Direction / DirectionCross / Rotation / RotationCross shapes (858 effects)
needs_translation_layer.why: Direction orients the quad along the particle's velocity (a streak, not a billboard); the Cross variants draw a second quad perpendicular to the first so the streak reads from any angle.
needs_translation_layer.suggestion: Direction is close to a stretched billboard - Godot has no built-in velocity-aligned billboard for 3D particles, so use a custom vertex shader that builds the quad from VELOCITY. For the Cross variants, use a two-quad cross MeshInstance as the draw pass with BILLBOARD_DISABLED.

needs_translation_layer.what: Indirect texturing / ETX1 (179 blocks, all of the 0x4000 and 0xC000 ids)
needs_translation_layer.why: This is a framebuffer read distorted by a scrolling normal map - the heat haze over torches and lava, and the arrow/sword blur. It is a screen-space effect, not a particle feature. The engine even patches the live framebuffer copy into the texture named 'AK_kagerouSwap00' (src/d/d_particle.cpp:635-642).
needs_translation_layer.suggestion: A quad with a shader using SCREEN_TEXTURE (hint_screen_texture) and a UV offset sampled from the indirect texture, using ETX1.mIndTexMtx as the distortion matrix and mExpScale as its exponent.

needs_translation_layer.why: Godot's ParticleProcessMaterial has gravity, damping, turbulence and attractor nodes - it has no swirl-about-an-axis or convection field.
needs_translation_layer.suggestion: A custom process shader. These are only 340 of 3696 field blocks, so they can be deferred: implement Gravity, Random, Drag, Magnet and Newton first and you have covered 3356 of 3696.

needs_translation_layer.what: KFA1 emitter-timeline curves (1143 blocks; 615 of them drive mRate)
needs_translation_layer.why: These animate the EMITTER over the emitter's own life - spawn rate ramping up then down, emission volume growing, particle lifetime shortening. Godot's curves all animate a property over an individual PARTICLE's life. Different axis entirely.
needs_translation_layer.suggestion: Drive them from GDScript in _process: sample the baked curve at (emitter_age_frames) and write GPUParticles3D.amount_ratio (for the rate curve) or the process material's parameters. amount_ratio is the natural target for KFA1 id 0.

needs_translation_layer.why: Toon effects are tinted at draw time by the ROOM's light colour (dKy_tevstr_c), which is why the same footstep dust looks warm indoors and cold at sea. The room number is smuggled in through the s8 setupInfo argument.
needs_translation_layer.suggestion: Multiply prmColor by the remake's current room/ambient light colour before handing it to the shader.

needs_translation_layer.why: The original caps at 3000 particles and 150 emitters globally and simply returns NULL past that (src/d/d_particle.cpp:649). A remake that spawns a GPUParticles3D per effect with a create_timer to free it - which is what Game.burst does today - will leak nodes under load.
needs_translation_layer.suggestion: Pool the emitter nodes and reuse them, matching the original's budget.

suggested_first_step.confidence: medium - this is a recommendation, not a finding
steps: 1. Add gcrip/formats/jpa.py (container walk + the 8 struct decoders in _data.format.blocks) and teach the ripper to extract files/res/Particle/*.jpc. The texture side needs no new code: TEX1+0x20 is a BTI header that gcrip.formats.bti already reads.
2. Export the ~40 distinct textures used by the common-bank effects in _priority to PNG (they are tiny - mostly 32x32 IA4) plus a flipbook atlas for the 260 animated ones.
3. Write one particle shader implementing the TEV presets in _godot.tev, with prm/env uniforms. Preset 3 alone covers 58% of the game's effects.

4. Write a JPA->GPUParticles3D builder that consumes the parsed JSON and builds the node at runtime, handling only Billboard/YBillboard/DirBillboard shapes and the Gravity/Random/Drag fields. That already covers 2346 of 3370 shape records and 2945 of 3696 field blocks.

5. Replace Game.burst at game.gd:2168 with the real death set - 0x0013 SIBOUBAKUEN + 0x0014 SIBOUPOFU + 0x0015 SIBOUSPIRIT + 0x0016 SIBOUFLASH - fired together, which is what d_a_disappear.cpp:79-88 does. That single change fixes all 7 existing burst() call sites.
6. Then the hit set (0x000D, 0x000C, 0x000F, 0x0010) and the footstep set (0x2022, 0x2027, 0x0023, 0x0024), which together are the most-fired effects in the game.
